Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Presentation: 45-year-old non-smoking woman with SLE on methotrexate presents with 1 day of dyspnea, pleuritic right-sided back pain on deep inspiration, subjective fever, and two episodes of hemoptysis. Reports ~2 weeks of fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance. Remote assessment suggests hemodynamic stability; oropharynx normal; no cervical lymphadenopathy.
- Clinician impression (transcript): Suspected chest infection/pneumonia; requires same-day in-person exam (vitals, chest auscultation) prior to initiating antibiotics.
- Differential diagnosis (aligned with DDx): Community-acquired pneumonia with pleurisy (more likely given fever, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, immunosuppression from methotrexate/SLE). Pulmonary embolism with pulmonary infarction also a consideration due to pleuritic pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis, and SLE-related VTE risk. Acute bronchitis possible but less favored due to localized pleuritic pain and immunosuppression. Other lower-likelihood considerations include SLE pleuritis and methotrexate-induced pneumonitis.
- Conflicts/notes: Patient name inconsistent in transcript (“Tracy Chapman” initially; later “Doris”)—conflict noted.

Management Plan
- Arrange same-day face-to-face review for full set of vitals (temperature, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation) and chest auscultation; assess stability.
- No antibiotics prescribed at this time; treatment to be determined after in-person assessment.
- If examination supports pneumonia, start appropriate antibiotic (no known allergies).
- Depending on findings and clinical course, possible follow-up chest X-ray if symptoms do not settle, per clinician discussion.
- Patient provided contact details to book the in-person appointment today.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Community-acquired pneumonia with pleurisy – High likelihood: Acute fever, pleuritic right-sided pain, dyspnea, minor hemoptysis; immunosuppression from methotrexate/SLE.
- Pulmonary embolism with pulmonary infarction – Moderate likelihood: Triad of pleuritic pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis; SLE increases VTE risk despite normal pulse and no classic provoking factors.
- Acute bronchitis – Moderate likelihood: Can cause acute cough, low-grade fever, and minor hemoptysis; less favored due to localized pleuritic pain and immunosuppression.
